@graph.name: Tray Packer
@graph.description: A tray packer is a top-load case packer that places trays of packaged product into shipping cases in a set pattern, as a robotic cell or as an integrated erect, pack and seal machine. TRF Industrial Automation packs trays with TRFRapidpack robotic case packing and with TRFOnepack, which also erects and seals the case . Your line setup and speed decide which one fits.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Tray Packer and a Tray Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tray packer loads trays into shipping cases at the case packing step. A tray palletizer stacks loaded trays directly onto a pallet at the palletizing step, for plants that ship trays without an outer case. Some plants need both, and TRF can engineer the case packer, the conveying and the palletizer as one project with shared controls.

mainEntity.name: Can a Tray Packer Handle Trays With Film Lids or Delicate Contents?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. Top loading lowers each tray into the case instead of pushing it, and TRFRapidpack is designed for controlled handling of delicate, flexible or irregularly shaped products. Where the tool may contact the tray, and how fast it may move, are defined during the application review with your real trays produced under normal line conditions.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Integrated Case Packer and Separate Erecting, Packing and Sealing Machines?

acceptedAnswer.text: An integrated case packer erects the case, loads it and seals it in one coordinated machine, with one controls platform. Separate machines each need their own interfaces, controls and floor space. TRFOnepack is the integrated option, for applications of about 20 to 50 products per minute, and it can start standalone and later join a complete TRF end-of-line system.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFRapidpack is designed for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the tray, the pick tool, the pack pattern and how trays leave the sealer, and TRF engineering validates it for each line before the design is closed.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. The signals and buffers between your tray sealer and the case packer, and the handoff to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Case Packer and a Case Erector?

acceptedAnswer.text: A case erector forms an open case from a flat blank, and a case packer loads products into that case. TRF supplies case erecting only as part of an integrated solution: TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals in one machine, and end-of-line projects with TRFRapidpack include case forming and closing, so one partner answers for the flow from flat case to sealed case.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: operators packing trays per shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, output the tray sealer gains when packing stops limiting it, trays damaged by handling and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
